summary: BurnBar uses official libsignal Double Ratchet for device-to-device and libsignal HPKE sealing at-rest on Mac/Android/daemon/backend, a homegrown Double Ratchet on every phone-to-AI-gateway lane, and an App-Store-clean libsignal-free iOS satellite that reads at-rest via CryptoKit HPKE.

claims.cryptokit-hpke-atrest: At-rest HPKE sealing (CryptoKit, RFC 9180, interoperable with the libsignal seal, no libsignal link)
claims.homegrown-double-ratchet: Hardened encrypted gateway (homegrown Double Ratchet, forward secrecy)

invariants: iOS never uses a libsignal-bearing model on any channel; its at-rest is cryptokit-hpke-atrest (CryptoKit RFC-9180 interop, no libsignal link) — the App-Store-clean hard rule.
device_to_device for macos/android/daemon must be libsignal-double-ratchet (official Signal Protocol); ios.device_to_device must be none-satellite; backend has no device_to_device channel.

ai_gateway must be homegrown-double-ratchet for every platform — never libsignal — because the gateway decrypts plaintext to run the model and the homegrown ratchet already provides forward secrecy and post-compromise security.
Marketing claims map strictly by model; iOS must never map to the 'Signal Protocol' claim.
